Make sure you have the correct fitting tool first and you should be okay. My suggestion was rap it with the hammer a couple good whacks right on top of the head solid and square. Go slow and if you feel like your not on it properly then you're not. Resituate yourself and get as much comfortable pul on it as you can. And just think if you break the head off of the bolt you get to use an easy out. ;)

Torx is designed to handle a lot of torque when the screwdriver is exactly the right size. If it's smaller, there's a chance it would strip the screw. But the right size screwdriver can take a lot of pressure without stripping the screw or the screwdriver. Philips head drivers are designed to cam out to prevent overtightening. Torx screwdrivers are not, so that you can tighten it as much as possible, and loosen tight screws.

Kroil is the best penetrating oil I have found. Knocker Loose is second and PB Blaster is third. Here is a good real world test: http://www.stovebolt.com/ubbthreads/ubbthreads.php?ubb=showflat&Number=215171 I base this on my own experience.

Also a heat wrench (propane or butane torch) works well. Heat the block and not the bolt. Spray a little Kroil and let it sit. Reheat the block. Touch the bolt with a piece of ice. The block expands away from the bolt from the heat and the ice shrinks the bolt. The heat/thaw will cause any rust to break loose. My local grocery store sells a small piece of dry ice cheap--use gloves when handling it.

Have patience. A impact socket as others have mentioned will help. Use it both directions to tighten and then loosen so the rust and crud is broken loose. Use a quality Torx socket. A cheap one of Chinesium can damage the head of the bolt. I have 1 swivel socket that I bought from the Snap-On truck for use on my Jeep. It is the only socket for the catalytic converter to exhaust manifold that will fit and is strong enough. And it cost about $40. Well worth it. So if you need one strong tool then buy it.
